title: Multi-dimensional ground reaction force vector analysis
author: Sarah Jane Hobbs
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.r3dd8i6

steps.title: Collect GRF Data
steps.instruction: Collect three-dimensional ground reaction force (GRF) data using a series of force platforms in line, or consecutive trials from one platform if speed is controlled within 0.1 m.s-1.

substeps.instruction: Habituate the horse prior to data collection.
Ensure trials are collected without interference from the handler.
Set sampling frequency to typically 960 or 1000 Hz.

steps.title: Process and Filter Force Data
steps.instruction: Clean and filter the collected GRF data to remove noise and isolate stance phases.

substeps.instruction: Use only clean hits for analysis.
Separate stance phases using a threshold between 50 and 100 N.
Remove noisy data or apply a 4th order Butterworth filter with a 100 Hz cut off frequency.

steps.title: Prepare Data for Visualization
steps.instruction: Downsample and extract GRF and centre of pressure (COP) data for vector plotting.

substeps.instruction: Downsample forces to between 120 and 250 Hz.
Extract 3D GRF and COP data into columns (e.g., text or ASCII formats).
Plot a vector diagram for each vector across the stance phase for each plane, with the origin at the COP, magnitude and orientation scaled to the planar GRF (refer to DOI: 10.7717/peerj.4399/supp-6).

steps.title: Calculate Summary Vector Variables
steps.instruction: Compute the vector magnitude and angle from the force data.

substeps.instruction: Calculate vector magnitude (VecMag) by dividing the vector summation of individual vectors by the number of samples contributing to the value.
Determine the angle of the summary vector (VecAng) using trigonometry from the components of the vector magnitude, expressed relative to the vertical (positive values directed cranially).

steps.title: Perform SPM Analysis
steps.instruction: Conduct Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) analysis on 1, 2, or 3 components of the GRF using the spm1d package (v. M.0.4.1) in Matlab or Python.

substeps.instruction: Normalize each stance phase, typically to 101 points, and calculate a mean for each limb.
Assemble data into vector fields (e.g., for 10 horses, 101 data points per stance phase, and two GRF components, create a 10 * 101 * 2 vector field).
Use Hotelling's T2 test for multivariate analysis of left and right forelimbs or hindlimbs.
Use a t-test for univariate analysis of a single GRF component for each limb.
Determine the critical threshold using Random Field Theory to control the type I error rate (alpha %).
Generate plots of the SPM trace(s) and comparisons of left and right limbs for each GRF component.
